Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund with automatic payments to all identifiable members. Fees and expenses would be paid separately, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded would go to the class. We are prepared to discuss the figures, but meaningful direct class recovery is essential.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments and meaningful direct recovery are important. Brightline can offer a $28 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can keep your proposed fee terms unchanged if Brightline increases the class fund to $30 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval. We will work with you to document the settlement promptly.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Thank you for your proposal. Brightline has reached a binding settlement agreement with counsel in a related action, subject to court approval, and is not making a counterproposal.

Keep any unawarded fees for the class and avoid terms that could trade class recovery for fee protection.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached a proposed settlement providing a $30 million class fund, automatic payments to identifiable class members, and a separate $5 million request for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any fees not awarded will go to the class, and Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Fees were addressed during the same negotiations as class relief, not only after class relief had been agreed. The settlement remains subject to the Court’s review under Rule 23(e).
